# Quality gate -> 1024 (v7: fully relative paths, batch stops properly)

Point `[2]` at any folder of source photos and queue once per image. Every
decision below is automatic and per-image; nothing needs staging between steps.

**Start command:** `./start.sh --nopin --disable-smart-memory --disable-dynamic-vram --lowvram --reserve-vram 4`
NOT `--lean` -- `--cache-none` breaks the lazy branches (see the README).

## The chain
1. **Score s1** `[20]`. Face < 200px, or skin with no sensor noise at all
   (illustration / airbrushed / AI) -> rejected outright, no SR wasted.
2. **Too small / soft / grainy** -> lazy **SeedVR2** `[21]`, rescore `[30]`,
   a second pass `[31]` if needed, final verdict `[40]`. SR target is chosen
   per image to land the face at ~800px.
3. **Head crop** `[50]`: derotated to eye level, square, +15% pad.
4. **B&W / sepia?** `[56]` -> lazy **DDColor** `[57]`, tagged `_col`.
5. **Single-hue colour wash?** `[79]` **SkinToneMatch** shifts Lab a/b so the
   SKIN lands on target; L untouched. Self-skips anything already multi-hued,
   so it only fires on DDColor's teal/orange or a genuinely cast photo.
6. **Texture below 1.0?** `[80]` -> lazy **SUPIR** `[83]-[88]`, tagged `_sup`.
7. **Face drifted?** `[91]` reverts to the pre-SUPIR crop if ArcFace < 0.90,
   tagged `_noid`.
8. **Still below 0.70?** `[90]` -> also tagged `_rev` for a human.
9. Save to `train/`.

So the filename tells you what happened: no tag = clean out of the box,
`_col` = colour is invented, `_sup` = SUPIR restored it, `_noid` = SUPIR
drifted the face and was thrown away, `_sup_rev` = SUPIR ran and it is still
marginal. Every scoring also appends to the CSV.

## Skin-tone target IS dataset-specific
`[79]` defaults to a 11 / b 14, the median of the a warm-toned set. The an East Asian set
measures **a 10.3 / b 9.2** -- `a` barely moves between datasets, `b` does, and
too high a `b` turns skin yellow. The survey script prints `skin_a`/`skin_b`
medians, so read them off any new corpus instead of guessing. Wire a reference
image into `[79]` to use that image's skin as the target instead.

## Paths are RELATIVE -- change `[2]` and nothing else
`[2]` takes **one directory per line**, and `current_dir` follows each image,
so a whole tree of model folders processes in one queue with every output
landing in its own folder:

| sink | goes to | set by |
|---|---|---|
| accepted crops | `<source dir>/train2` | `[92]` |
| rejected | `<source dir>/gate_rejected` | the node below `[92]` |
| gate CSV | `<source dir>/quality_gate.csv` | the node below that |

Change a suffix in those StringConcatenate nodes to rename an output. Nothing
in the graph carries an absolute dataset path, so retargeting to the East Asian
set means editing `[2]` -- and `[79]`'s `target_b` to 9 (see below).

**Never point an output suffix at the source dir itself** -- the loader
re-globs every run, so saving beside the inputs makes the batch grow forever.
Re-survey a new set before trusting the thresholds:
`uv run python ~/comfy_common/tools/portrait_quality_survey.py <dir>`

## Thresholds (from a 419-image survey; tune in [20]/[30]/[40])
| metric | pass | notes |
|---|---|---|
| face_px | >= 500 (hard floor 200) | face bbox short edge, NATIVE pixels |
| clarity | >= 60 | ~20 soft, ~60 acceptable, 150+ crisp |
| grain | <= 2.5 | source noise; also >= 0.15 or it is not a photograph |
| chroma | < 5 = mono | B&W <3; sepia 3-8 with hue_spread <0.45 |
| texture | >= 0.85 post-crop | below -> SUPIR; wax <0.55, real pores 1.2-2.5 |

## Why SUPIR and not a normal img2img
Ordinary img2img at 1024 is capped by the VAE: a pure encode->decode through
`ae.sft` costs -0.04 with no sampling at all, so Chroma, Flux.1, Flux.2, SRPO
and Qwen all returned the input or worse. SUPIR has a purpose-trained denoise
encoder that replaces the VAE encoder for the hint latent, so its conditioning
skips that low-pass. Measured 0.63 -> 0.87 at 20s/image, identity 0.941.
**`[87]` denoise is a PEAK at 0.65** -- 0.75 collapses to 0.62. Do not raise it.

## Why there is no loopback (tested)
- **A second SUPIR pass makes it worse**: 0.45 -> 0.36 on a retry candidate.
- **Retrying at another denoise does not rescue a failure**: d0.45/0.55/0.65 all
  landed within 0.03 of each other, all below the input. The peak does not move
  usefully per image, so there is nothing for a retry stage to find.
- The SR stage IS already an unrolled loop (s1 -> SR -> s2 -> SR -> s3) and is
  at its limit: the 2048 cap means a second pass stops growing the face
  (measured 248 -> 424 -> 425 px).

## Why the gate is 1.0, not 0.85
SUPIR converges everything toward ~0.7-1.0 -- it lifts low texture and PULLS
DOWN high texture. Measured over 89 colourised crops:

| started at | mean after | improved |
|---|---|---|
| < 0.70 | 0.56 -> 0.72 | 17/20 |
| 0.70-0.85 | 0.78 -> 0.99 | 18/23 |
| 0.85-1.10 | 0.97 -> 1.08 | 21/31 |
| > 1.10 | 1.36 -> 1.35 | 7/15 |

Above ~1.1 it is a coin flip that costs 20s and risks replacing real detail
with synthesis. 1.0 is the conservative line: everything below it reliably
gains, everything above keeps what it already has.

## Ending a batch
Queue with the **batch-count** field next to the Queue button, not the
"instant" auto-queue. Either works now -- `MultiDirImageBatch` rejects an
exhausted batch at *validation* time, so surplus runs never enter the queue
and auto-queue cannot spin -- but batch count tells you the exact number up
front. `[2]` logs the image count on the first image of a run.

## Forcing individual images through
`[5] FORCE`: `accept` / `refine_1x` / `refine_2x` ignore every threshold.
Put the stragglers in their own folder, point `[2]` at it, set it, queue,
then set it back to `off`.

## Known gaps
- DDColor invents hair colour on highlighted dark hair -- eyeball `_col` files.
- No watermark detection.
- Identity caps are reported by the survey, not enforced here.
- The texture metric cannot tell pores from dither; it has been fooled twice.
  Check `_sup` output at 1:1 before trusting a threshold change.
- Don't add/remove files in the source dir mid-queue; the loader indexes by
  sorted position.
